A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same B-Free research paper. Text, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary material support comparison; v1 supplementary Sections 8–13 correspond to v2 Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector evaluations, training-data and architecture ablations, calibration results, and robustness experiments in both the main paper and supplement.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of the revised detector, additional controlled comparisons, and results on two autoregressive generators, alongside retained experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4 and the implementation appendix replace the SigLIP backbone and two fully connected layers with self-supervised DINOv2, four registers, and one fully connected layer. The self-conditioned generation and inpainting dataset construction remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds evaluation on 2,000 images from two additional autoregressive generators. Existing training datasets and benchmark coverage remain, including FakeBench and PolarDiffShield. The 1,400-image, 100-day online-image study already appears in v1's supplement.

E2.justification: The 15-detector comparator set in the main benchmark tables is retained. v2 Figure 11 adds DMID, DeFake, AntifakePrompt, RINE, and CoDE to the Synthbuster corruption comparison, previously limited to proposed-method variants. Table 3 also introduces basic DINOv2 as an architecture comparator.

E3.justification: Headline evaluations switch from SigLIP with 512-pixel inputs to DINOv2 with 504-pixel crops, and the reference augmentation changes from inpainted+ to inpainted++. The D3 training-data comparison also changes backbone. These are revised experimental configurations; the principal evaluation metrics and optimizer settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds reconstruction-with-inpainting controls, comparisons of DINOv2 with and without registers, and direct corruption-robustness comparisons with other detectors. The D3 ablation is revised. RINE's training-data analysis survives as aggregate results, while its per-generator breakdown and separate online and FakeInversion augmentation comparisons are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Both present point estimates, with the same calibration-error reporting practice.

E6.justification: For the revised detector configuration, headline average bAcc/NLL changes from 89.9/0.28 to 96.3/0.10 (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 5). GenImage bAcc changes from 91.4 to 89.3, including BigGAN from 94.6 to 68.7. New autoregressive results report 99% AUC and 94.2% accuracy. These compare different backbone/augmentation configurations; the main baseline scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The ECE and balanced NLL definitions in Equations 1–2 remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical derivation or assumption.

C1.justification: The central contributions concerning semantic alignment, content augmentation, generalization, and calibration remain. The introduction strengthens its quantitative accuracy claim from 87% to above 90% on unseen generators; the abstract's main claims and the conclusion remain substantially stable.

C2.justification: v2 tentatively explains register benefits through preservation of local patch information and autoregressive generalization through tokenizer similarity to Stable Diffusion embeddings. It also revises the earlier interpretation that the strongest augmentation is chiefly necessary online. The stated limitations concerning fundamentally different generators and adversarial attacks remain.

D1.justification: v2 states that code and data are publicly available, replacing v1's promised release, and updates the documented backbone, classifier head, crop size, and padding threshold. Hardware, optimizer hyperparameters, batch size, and early-stopping instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for DINOv2, Vision Transformers Need Registers, and the two autoregressive generators. The related-work taxonomy and positioning against semantic-alignment and autoencoder-only approaches remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section framework remains, with targeted introduction, method, and interpretation edits. RINE summaries and the extended online-image analysis move into the main discussion; supplementary sections become Appendices A–F, and references move after the appendices.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, expands Figure 6, removes the standalone seven-day augmentation plot, and brings a redesigned 100-day comparison into Figure 8. It adds the corruption comparison in Figure 11 and splits or recombines architecture and training-data ablation tables, substantially reorganizing the experimental displays.

improvement.justification: New reconstruction-plus-inpainting and architecture controls better support the explanations for B-Free's effectiveness, while direct corruption comparisons strengthen the robustness evidence. Updated implementation and access reporting also help reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removed detailed ablation breakdowns and uneven generalization of the revised detector, particularly the BigGAN decline; the overall improvement is limited.
